title: REVE: A Foundation Model for EEG – Adapting to Any Setup with Large-Scale Pretraining on 25,000 Subjects
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Four-class motor-imagery classification: left fist, right fist, both fists and feet; the original PhysioNet-MI downstream endpoint, not MAE reconstruction or few-shot transfer.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Four-class motor-imagery classification: left fist, right fist, both fists and feet; the original PhysioNet-MI downstream endpoint, not MAE reconstruction or few-shot transfer.

Source-paper comparison for PhysioNet-MI four-class balanced accuracy: Balanced accuracy is mean class recall, (1/4) sum_c TP_c/(TP_c+FN_c), higher is better. Cohen kappa and weighted F1 are separately reported supporting metrics, not substitute winning endpoints.
success_criteria: Recover and bind the precise Table 12 preprocessing, all eligible epochs, original run aggregation and REVE-Base access.

Exceed the source-paper balanced accuracy and a calibrated author rerun under identical original subjects, runs, labels, preprocessing and inputs, by the predeclared justified effect with uncertainty.
Freeze candidate and hyperparameters using only participants 1–89 before final evaluation on all source test participants 90–109.
Do not treat better frozen-feature, few-shot, altered-montage, smaller-cohort or new-split results as a Table 12 paper win.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
